summary: K4/S8/S7 are sound modulo the explicitly unproved A4 and named imported results; G6 is a complete unconditional geometry classification. No claim that A4 or P6 is proved.

input_scope.dependencies: Read listed local dependency documents; check N10/N11/N12/E2/Z18/A4/S4 application hypotheses. Existing imported theorem chains are not recursively certified anew. paper.txt read Theorem 8 and C1-C3 passages.

micro_obligations.note: F arbitrary complete-graph matching; a even by parity-changing translation; no bipartiteness assumption is used.
Free y: adding ay leaves an opposite-parity two-hole matching; N10 root at one remaining hole and short-neighbor target has parity of the other. Closing and deleting ay preserves all F.
Covered y: replace yk by ka. Hole set replaces a by y independently of parity(k), hence one even and three odd holes. A4 can omit y.
Opening ka and restoring ky recovers all original long edges; choosing a short-neighbor y closes a 32-vertex path to a cycle without duplicating its endpoint edge.
An adjacent non-root hole pair can be joined while keeping u free; Z18 applies to the resulting short four-hole matching for the same opposite-parity target.

For each candidate mirror of a B odd hole, the original cross-neighbor is free; absent original hole adjacency it is internally covered unless it is u. After replacement only at most one of three candidates can be a cross-port; at least two are internal.
A has one hole v, so c is odd. F=M_A*-bk has no half-layer and within A minus v,b has Y=X_A plus k, with even size c+1>=4.
N12 supplies W; k pairs with a in X_A. D=W-ak avoids a,b and N11 compression is precisely F+W, with v odd and b even.
Removing matching D from a-b path yields nontrivial vertex-disjoint segments. Real cross-edges and bw yield R on X_B plus w, disjoint from M_B*. The remaining holes are z,q,s,t, balanced for K4.
For c>=2, F has Y=X_A plus z,k of even size >=4. W(k) lies in X_A or is z. N11 applies also when a=z; endpoint set after deleting D is X_A plus z,b.
y=z xor e_i is odd, is not a B original hole or u,h, and is internally covered; hence R and M_B* overlap exactly at y.
r=M_B*(y) is outside R endpoints, d=R(y) is outside M_B* endpoints other than y; replacing yr,yd by rd is legal. Exactly q,s,t,y become holes, of type one even/three odd.
A4 omits y; rd expands as ry followed by y-d transfer segment. Every A-v vertex and B vertex is recovered once, including any real long cross-edge hu.
For c=0, a=z and D empty. Tb free of half-layers is exactly the N11 condition; no use of N12 with two free points is made.
At most one half-layer is possible in M_A*: a half-layer forces all short edges into its direction and both half-layers of that direction would cover free v.

For c>=2, no half-layer or a half-layer touching an internally covered candidate yields the first-stage deletion. A noninternal candidate cannot touch a matching half-layer, so the residual real half-layer avoids all three candidates.

For c=0 and hu in A, v,h,u all lie in A: otherwise original vh is a remaining true cross-edge. All original M edges avoid cut i. paper.txt Theorem 8 applies with n=6, at most five directions; C1-C3 all require u covered and thus fail.
For c=0 and hu in B, M_A*=M_A is short, with holes v,z; the three even candidates have distinct short matching edges and odd partners.

If each Tb has a half-layer, each contributes >=7 old short edges; Te retains >=6 of them. All its short edges must follow its half-layer direction, forcing common direction. Omission of v forces the same half-layer H.
The common H avoids every candidate b. In Te for e!=b, bk_b is retained, so k_b cannot be in H. Thus zk_b cannot be in H, which proves H is contained in original M_A and avoids z as well as v.
The complement of H gives equal j-bits for z and all candidates, opposite the j-bit of v. Since j!=i, these are exactly the j-bits of w,s,t.
E2 applies to the same complete-graph matching M* omitting v, n=6>=4. Recut target side A_j has no half-layer and at least eight real cross-edges; z,w,s,t are on its opposite side.
Only q may join v after recut. If q does, invoke already-proved first-stage c>=2 case; otherwise one-hole side has odd c>=9 and invokes already-proved S8. No recursive appeal to S7.

For any differing coordinate of z,q, nonconstant W gives one/two W points on each target side, hence S4. Thus W is constant on every coordinate in D. Three distinct same-parity points require >=3 remaining coordinates; positive even |D| is therefore two.

Translation by even z preserves parity and adjacency, permutation sends q to 3; low-bit r=3 is reduced by xor3 exchanging even holes, and r=2 by swapping low coordinates. All reductions act on v and u too.

r=0 forces all high words to weight three. r=1 permits only weights two/four. Three edges on four vertices have precisely triangle, star, path types; with the weight-four word the remaining two edges are adjacent or disjoint. Six rows exhaust W.

High columns give S4 iff v_j=1 and c_j=2; low columns add S7 exactly when v_i differs from r_i. Include v odd and outside W. Table yields 1+1+5+2+2+1=12 pairs, without claiming minimal target/root orbits.

The chosen root is any even point outside the two non-root even holes, at most 30; it is not enumerated. No matching feasibility assertion or path-existence conclusion follows from the geometry enumeration.
